title: Enhanced orbital-angular-momentum dimensionality and spatial-spectral decoupling in thin-film SPDC
authors: Dmitrii Akatev, Jakub Lewandowski, Maria Chekhova
abstract: Thin-film spontaneous parametric down-conversion, due to the relaxed phase-matching condition, generates photon pairs that are extremely broadband in frequency and angle and highly entangled in time/frequency and position/momentum. Here we show that it also provides a very broad orbital angular momentum (OAM) spectrum, which, in contrast to the case of bulk crystals, is decoupled from the frequency spectrum. To demonstrate it experimentally, we generate photon pairs in a $7~μ\mathrm{m}$-thick lithium niobate film and compare them with those from a $500~μ\mathrm{m}$-thick periodically poled lithium niobate crystal under identical pump conditions. The thin-film source exhibits a substantially broader OAM spectrum, with the azimuthal Schmidt number almost 9 times larger than that of the bulk source. On this highly entangled state, we perform quantum-state tomography in selected two- and four-dimensional OAM subspaces, demonstrating high-purity maximally entangled states. These results highlight thin nonlinear films as a promising platform for high-dimensional quantum-state generation with weak spatial--spectral coupling.
summary: This work experimentally shows that using thin-film nonlinear crystals enhances the orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) spectrum generated via SPDC compared to bulk crystals. Crucially, the thin film achieves a decoupling between the OAM spectrum and the photon frequency, enabling the creation of high-purity, high-dimensional entangled quantum states.
main_problem: The paper aims to demonstrate and exploit enhanced orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) dimensionality and the decoupling of spatial and spectral entanglement in spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC).
main_result: Thin-film SPDC sources generate photon pairs with a substantially broader OAM spectrum compared to bulk crystals, exhibiting near spatial-spectral decoupling, which is crucial for high-dimensional quantum state generation.
method: The study uses quantum-state tomography in selected OAM subspaces and compares OAM spectra measured via the phase-flattening technique between thin-film and bulk crystal sources.
model_or_system: The experiment compares photon pair generation in a thin-film lithium niobate (LN) film against a bulk periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) crystal, utilizing the thin-film approximation where the thickness is much smaller than the coherence length.
key_observables: Azimuthal Schmidt number ($K_{az}$), OAM spectrum width, state purity ($P$), and state fidelity ($F$).
important_parameters: Thin-film thickness ($\sim 7 \mu	ext{m}$), bulk crystal thickness ($\sim 500 \mu	ext{m}$), and the comparison under identical pump conditions.
main_assumptions: The thin-film approximation ($L \ll L_{coh}$) is key, and the comparison relies on identical pump conditions.
figures_summary: Figures compare the transverse-momentum amplitude (TPA) and joint OAM spectra between thin-film and bulk sources, demonstrating the superior OAM bandwidth of the thin film.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical basis for thin-film SPDC, presents experimental measurements comparing OAM spectra and TPA against bulk sources, and concludes with quantum state tomography results confirming high-purity, high-dimensional entanglement.
why_interesting: The demonstration of spatial-spectral decoupling in a solid-state source is highly relevant for developing scalable, high-dimensional quantum light sources for quantum communication and computation.

Figure 4 shows the frequency-resolved OAM spectra of the thin-film LN (a) and bulk ppLN crystal (b), calculated using the approach described in Section 3. All spectra were normalized to the probability of the ℓ= 0 mode at zero frequency detuning, 𝑃0(0). The thin LN film features a constant OAM spectrum across all the SPDC bandwidth, whereas the bulk ppLN exhibits a pronounced variation of the OAM distribution with frequency. This behaviour is consistent with spatial–spectral decoupling in the thin-film source, in contrast to the bulk PPLN crystal.
